subtype: Approach: rehearse an earthquake drill at home [Thinking]
passage:
Deepak: So you turned the living room into a drill ground?

Sumit: Kind of! My thinking was simple. In a real shake I won't have time to think, so my body has to already know. I chose the dining table because the legs are thick and it's away from the glass cabinet. Then I checked the two ways out, the front door and the service stairs, and made sure nothing was stacked in front of them. Drop, cover, hold on: down on my knees, under the table, one hand on a leg. My younger brother and sister thought it was a game, so I let them time each other. We did it three Sundays in a row. The third time neither of them asked why any more, they just dropped.

qa.q: Which piece of furniture did Sumit choose for cover?
What did Sumit believe about how the body reacts in a real earthquake?
qa.a: Sumit believed there would be no time to think, so the body has to already know what to do, which shows a wish to feel ready rather than helpless.

qa.q: What could Sumit add to make the drill stronger, and why?
qa.a: Sumit could practise at a different time or in the dark, because a real shake will not wait for a convenient moment.

qa.q: How might Sumit's younger brother see the drill?
qa.a: Sumit's younger brother probably saw it as a game at first, then felt safer as it became automatic.

grounding: Illustrates practising drop, cover and hold on at home, choosing a sturdy table and exits and teaching younger siblings, so panic becomes a learned response.
